node.label: Anthony D. Smith
node.date_label: The Ethnic Origins of Nations (1986) · National Identity (1991) · Warwick opening, “Nations and their pasts” (1995) · Nationalism and Modernism (1998)
node.description: Explains particular nationalisms through ethnic ties, inherited memories, myths and symbols while acknowledging the modernity of most nations and nationalist movements. His Warwick opening praises Gellner’s contribution but argues that a general account of modernization leaves the content and intensity of particular cases unexplained. Smith explicitly declines to require one definite antecedent ethnic community for every nation. His ethno-symbolic approach therefore differs from a claim that all modern nations are unchanged survivals of antiquity. The debate with Gellner is presented through the participants’ own formulations, including their concessions and disagreements.
node.representative_figures_and_works: The Ethnic Origins of Nations (1986); National Identity (1991); Warwick opening “Nations and their pasts” (1995; published 1996); Nationalism and Modernism (1998).

proposed_edges.relationship: Uses ethnic ties, myths, memories and symbols to investigate the content and appeal of particular nationalisms.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Primary Smith opening, definitions and ethno-symbolic sections; reuses earlier qualified review, with opening/central paragraphs freshly read. He acknowledges most nations’ modernity and does not require a definite prior ethnic community in every case.

proposed_edges.relationship: Challenges the sufficiency of Gellner’s general modernist explanation for historically specific national attachments while acknowledging his intellectual contribution.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Directly named Warwick opening: critique of explanatory scope rather than denial of all modern conditions. Smith describes an approach/perspective and limits theoretical certainty; no unchanging ethnic essence or field consensus. Gellner’s reply remains separate.
